R7BH-bear-backcountry-0002.name: 670 m SW of Ten Mile Lake
R7BH-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Burn from 2018 (fire R92033), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 80 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Lower Post, about 42 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.99831, -129.05375, pull off on pullout (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 25 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 374 m, about 546 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m SW of the spot at 627 m (59.85531, -128.70021). Water: unnamed wetland 150 m E (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
